# The Companyof the Nightwake

*Pages PDF 106-111*

## **The Company of the Nightwake**
## **Predatory Ventures**
When _Nightwake_ appears on the horizon, few can be sure whether it heralds death and chains, or trade and silver. The vessel’s commander, Captain Nyandra Filvanir, delights in unsettling lesser creatures with uncertainty; she finds that disguising her intent makes them much more pliable. 

Naggaroth is a bleak land which cannot produce everything the dark elves demand, so they turn to trade for those luxuries, exotic goods, and commodities that are easier to take with silver than with the sword. Captain Filvanir commands a crew of piratical corsairs who raid and plunder with as much enthusiasm as their fellows in _Temple of Spite_ ’s fleet. Yet _Nightwake_ is also the flagship of a small flotilla of cargo vessels, wrackhold ships carrying goods to trade with anyone willing to deal with dark elves. 

Accompanying Filvanir is the merchant Anuidethar Veilthorn. Few places in the Old World are comfortable trading with dark elves, but he knows merchants in most of them. Brutal Norscans in Skjold and Kirkjugarður Langskipa offer iron, amber, captives, and strange beasts. Certain secluded ports on the Kislev, Empire, and Bretonnian coasts are willing to deal with _Nightwake_ , motivated by greed and fear in equal measure. Estalians and Tileans are amenable to Veilthorn’s charm and wares, providing the corsairs show restraint. Both Filvanir and Veilthorn are acquainted with several pirate lords of Sartosa, who understand better than most how the dark elves combine business with violence. 

Other reavers question why Filvanir and her crew do not just take what they want, rather than negotiate with lesser beings. Her answer is simple: you can only kill or capture once, but you can trade over and over until they have nothing left. Then you can kill them. 

## **Goals**
As both corsairs and traders, the crew of _Nightwake_ and its accompanying vessels have more complex goals than mere piracy. 

**Acquire wealth.** Dark elf society has a rigid hierarchy and there are precious few ways to elevate one’s status. Money cannot buy noble blood, but it can make life easier and safer, and so Filvanir’s corsairs and crew are united by greed — they want to amass a fortune to pay for prestige back in Clar Karond. 

**Make a profit.** To get rich, Veilthorn brokers lucrative trade. To buy at low prices, Filvanir might offer veiled threats or protection from more predatory dark elves. To sell high, they might ensure scarcity by cutting off supplies from other merchants. Veilthorn walks a fine line, driving profit through sharp practice without deterring trading partners from ever dealing with him again. 

**Acquire desirable goods.** Important elves on _Temple of Spite_ whisper that Captain Filvanir can acquire anything for the right price. By taking orders from the powerful, Filvanir secures wealth, favours, and influence in the close society of the ark. 

**Grow the fleet.** Filvanir currently commands three vessels, but she wants more cargo ships and more ravenships. She solicits investment from Clar Karond and members of the Black Convocation to make this happen. 

**Seek adventure.** Filvanir, Veilthorn, and the corsairs are restless and grow bored easily. If they can try something new in service of profit or plunder, they embrace the adventure. 

## **Rivals and Allies**
Captain Filvanir and her crew are in good standing with the fleetmaster, because he believes she supported him in the attempted mutiny. That is _partly_ true. She secretly backed Captain Kranthar Mancleaver, and while most conspirators died in the subsequent purge, a few survived. Now, Filvanir is being blackmailed, the highborn Lady Karasashalla has revealed that she knows of the captain’s association with mutineers and demands regular payments for her continued silence. 

Some of the more traditional dark elves think _Nightwake’s_ crew are weak because they would rather negotiate than kill or enslave other species. Captain Qulla feels this way and often mutters cutting remarks during meetings of the Reavers’ Council. Filvanir believes Qulla is merely jealous, and the fleetmaster and Captain Flariel find their exchanges amusing. The Khainites are also openly disdainful of Filvanir’s endeavours. 

Other powerful figures resent Anuidethar because of their business dealings — not everything provided by the merchant meets the promised quality standards, and investments are not guaranteed to pay back. Lord Skarrasha is a cold one knight who plots revenge on Filvanir and Veilthorn after he purchased a helm of supposedly Caledorian origin, which he later learned was forged in Karond Kar. 

_Nightwake_ has few friends in its favoured ports, just recurring trading partners who place little trust in the dark elves. Eyri Goldfinger of the Bjornlings is a match for Veilthorn’s negotiations and welcomes their arrival in Skjold, though he keeps his huscarls close. 

## **On the Black Ark**
Captain Filvanir maintains richly-decorated chambers in the Chain Spire, where she receives visitors for discreet discussions over rich Ulthuan wine. Only a few highborn deign to be seen associating with trade, but few can resist the possibilities of doing business with Filvanir. 

Anuidethar Veilthorn resides in Aelrath-Kar, alongside the more affluent merchants and dealmakers. Most of _Nightwake’s_ corsairs reside in quarters in the Tower of Trellech. Cargo and plunder from their ventures are kept in storage under the Tower of Trellech, protected by corsairs. 

When the corsairs return with holds full of goods and plunder, Veilthorn hosts an auction. The choice items go to Helbane and the Black Convocation, but what remains is always interesting to those with enough coin. These auctions are popular occasions, and gossip circulates the ark about what’s on offer. 

Kaia Fanmaris of Laurelorn Forest deals with the dark elves reluctantly. As ruler of the Ward of Storm, the ‘Stormwitch’ resents their appearances at Se-Athil as a necessary evil. Despite the accusations of cityborn in Tor Lithanel, she believes pragmatism must prevail — placating Captain Filvanir (and therefore Helbane) keeps _Temple of Spite_ ’s warhost at bay. 

## **Trade with the Eonir**
The Laurelorn forest produces rare goods and artefacts that dark elves cannot easily take by force. Rare herbs, minerals, and relics from before the Sundering are valued in naggaroth, so dark elves are willing to trade for them. although eonir relations with Ulthuan are strained, they know the Druchii have embraced their species’ darker side. eonir trade with dark elves is perhaps more concerned with self-preservation than wealth. 

## **Internal Tensions**
Most disputes within _Nightwake’s_ crew relate to sharing the wealth. Veilthorn privately feels that he does most of the work while Filvanir takes more than her share of the profit, while many of the crew think Veilthorn is a coward who relies on his silver tongue whilst they are willing to spill blood. Captains Delmier and Finscar of the wrackholds believe the corsairs look down on them, which they do. 

When times are good and everyone feels wealthy, these resentments are quietened. When a deal goes badly or misfortune strikes, open conflict is possible. 

## **The Dragons Below and the Lord of Murder**
Druchii seafarers are as superstitious as their human counterparts. They pray to mathlann for deliverance from his violent moods and invoke ‘the Dragons Below’, the god’s many children, which dwell in the depths. filvanir’s corsairs feel an allegiance to anath Raema, for they believe that whether hunting for victims or profit, they must be audacious and ruthless. 

. There are undercurrents of religious disquiet on _Nightwake_ Corsair arbeth Slad is a devout khainite who feels filvanir and Veilthorn have turned from the Druchii’s true master. he believes they have turned to amecs, a sea elf god of trade who would rather treat lesser species as equals than chattel and sacrifices. Slad proselytises quietly to his fellow corsairs with support from _Temple of Spite’_ s khainite hierarchy. 

## **Meeting the Company of the Nightwake**
The Characters could meet Captain Filvanir and her crew in one of the shadier ports in the Old World or Lustria, where they could witness _Nightwake_ sailing in to trade. They might encounter them in places like Mousillon, Skjold, Se-Athil, or even Hargendorf on a dark night. Veilthorn does most of the talking and drives a hard bargain, though the elves are rich and willing to spend. If they Characters have (or can acquire) a cargo the Nightwake desires, this could prove a lucrative encounter. 

The Characters could meet _Nightwake_ at sea. If their ship looks vulnerable, Captain Filvanir shouts an order to attack and board their vessel, taking cargo and captives. If the Characters’ ship presents a hard target, Veilthorn sees an opportunity to trade, or at least approach under a flag of truce. 

On _Temple of Spite_ , the crew of _Nightwake_ use the Characters to work as go-betweens with traders reluctant to deal with dark elves, or they might be useful in sourcing a rare artefact or commodity they seek for a wealthy patron. In these circumstances, the Characters receive an offer they can’t refuse. 

## **Disposition**
Captain Filvanir’s command includes three ships and their crews. They fly the Iron Talon banner of Clar Karond alongside Helbane’s personal banner, and Filvanir’s own ensign of golden dragon wings on an indigo field. 

- **Captain Filvanir** commands _Nightwake_ , a ravenship. Her second-in-command is Myria Drakemere, a scarred elf of few words who holds the crew to a very high standard of discipline. 

- The crew consists of 19 Corsairs, 14 ship’s crew and 2 lookouts — younger dark elves given the most menial tasks on board. Corsairs are the first to fight in a boarding action, the rest of the time they man the vessel alongside the ship’s crew. 

- **Anuidethar Veilthorn** travels on _Nightwake_ with his two scriveners, Hemiar and Phylia. These clerks keep the ships’ cargo manifests and attend to the ledgers. Veilthorn treats them as general dogsbodies who tend to his needs and write down his every idea. 

- _Endeavour’s Reward_ is a wrackhold commanded by **Captain Morwen Delmier** , with 20 sailors and 4 Corsairs to make sure they do as Filvanir says. Delmier wants to make enough money to buy her ship and leave Filvanir’s service forever. 

- **Captain Finskar** is an old seahand and near unshakeable at the helm. He captains the wrackhold _Morleth’s Shade_ with 20 sailors and 2 Corsairs. Filvanir trusts Finskar, as his wife and son serve on _Nightwake_ as sailors. 

- All three vessels have a crew of 80 captive oarsmen who rotate between ships, overseen by 2 Beastmasters. The majority are dwarfs, an expensive investment. Filvanir insists that you get what you pay for, as dwarfs can pull for longer on smaller rations and are less likely to die of disease or fatigue than humans. 

## **Appearance**
Filvanir’s corsairs wear traditional sea dragon hide cloaks and thick clothes. During boarding actions or a raid, they wear light armour for protection. The captain insists they dress in indigo with gold trim on their armour, in honour of her heraldry. 

In battle they cry _‘Chalcoi na mensha khelthrai!’_ which is a rough equivalent of ‘Gold or bloody death!’ in Druhir. 

## **Wheeling and Dealing — Easy Encounter**
This event can happen in any dubious port. The dark elves arrive at twilight to take advantage of their night vision. _Nightwake_ and _Morleth’s Shade_ are in dock, as Anuidethar Veilthorn negotiates to buy copper from local a merchant. 

The party overhears Veilthorn arguing with the merchant in a covered market away from the docks. Three corsairs stand behind him to intimidate the copper trader and, while Veilthorn’s words are good-humoured, his tone is threatening. The local merchant is holding out, but a **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test reveals a tremor of nerves in his voice. 

If the party hails _Nightwake_ , Vania assesses their strength. If they have nothing obvious to offer, she ignores them. If they seem weak and worth boarding, she chases them down when her crew return. 

If their ship looks dangerous, she offers to trade — Nightwake carries 200 Enc of fine Tiranoc marble (Base Price 6). Vania’s Haggle Test is taken at −2 SL given her circumstances. If she sells for −10% Base Price or less, the fully-crewed Nightwake pursues the party’s ship to recover the goods (unless it far outclasses a raven ship). 

## On Board _Nightwake_ :
The Characters could intervene, stepping in to haggle with Veilthorn and backing up the local merchant. Veilthorn welcomes the sport, while the corsairs are annoyed. This means they can Assist an **Opposed Haggle** Test, with the merchant’s Haggle Skill at 65. They could use Intimidate against Veilthorn, who will be Assisted by his corsair escort. 

If Veilthorn loses, he accepts the price and heads back to _Morleth’s Shade_ to arrange loading. If he wins, he swaggers back. Should the situation escalate into a fight, Veilthorn lets the corsairs engage. If the party lose, the corsairs leave them bleeding to teach the locals a lesson. If the dark elves lose, they retreat to _Nightwake_ and leave, vengeance on their minds. 

Alternately, this could turn into a business transaction. Veilthorn is looking to buy any metals, grain, or luxury goods. He bears no grudge if the Characters can make a deal with him. 

- Anuidethar Veilthorn 

- 3 Corsairs (wearing armour but no helmets) 

## **A Handful of Hands — Medium Encounter**
_Nightwake_ is anchored alone off an uncharted rocky island _._ Many of the crew are ashore, hunting fresh meat, while captives cut timber and fetch fresh water. The island is two miles long and heavily wooded. 

A lookout spots the party’s ship and informs Captain Filvanir. Many of her crew are on the island at least 15 minutes away, which leaves her with a dilemma. The Characters cannot tell how many dark elves are below decks. 

If the Party attack, Myria Drakemere sounds a horn to summon everyone back from the island. Filvanir orders corsairs to fire the Reapers and weigh anchor — hoping to sweep around the island, gather her crew and retaliate. It takes the corsairs 1d10+3 rounds to haul anchor and unfurl the sails. 

- Captain Filvanir and First Officer Myria Drakemere 0 8 Corsairs, 10 ship’s crew, and 1 lookout 

## **Everything Went South… — Hard Encounter**
The party happen across the aftermath of a failed negotiation, at an isolated location in the Old World. A local merchant arranged to buy arms and wine from _Nightwake_ , avoiding the local port to save on taxes. Negotiations went badly and Filvanir’s corsairs attacked the merchant and his guards, intending to take them as captives. 

Arrayed on a stony beach are 20 corsairs, wiping blood from their blades. Two bodies lie on the ground as a beastmaster chains eight more captives, including a well-dressed man protesting weakly. Filvanir and Veilthorn look on, as the scriveners count coins from a large sack of gold. Filvanir’s ships are anchored 50 yards offshore and two longboats are on the beach. 

The party could try to get help — roll a Perception Test for the corsairs to see them, modified by the Characters’ position and behaviour. They could attack and attempt to free the captives. Or they might try to negotiate if they have leverage, such as valuables or useful information. 

On the beach: 

- Captain Filvanir, Anuidethar Veilthorn, Hemiar, and Phylia the scriveners 

- 20 Corsairs 0 6 ship’s crew 

The remainder of Filvanir’s command are on the three ships. _Nightwake_ can fire three reaper bolt throwers at the beach. More corsairs jump in tidescourges at the first sign of trouble and take four rounds to row to shore. 

## **Captain Nyandra Filvanir, Dark Elf Reaver**
Captain Filvanir is an elf who knows gold can buy almost anyone. In her many years at sea, she has grown to see that status comes from what (and who) she can buy, regardless of the consequences. She runs her enterprise with the same cold efficiency she demands of her crew — each elf, sail, and nail are just cogs in the machinery of profit.

## **Armour**
Filvanir believes that to stay ahead, you must adapt. If the nobles are desperate for saurian ivory, you find it cheap and sell it high. If the Norscan will not trade whale oil at a decent price, you follow them and take it. It’s nothing personal and she has no special love for battle… it’s just business. She lets Anuidethar do the fast talking and negotiation, while she takes most of the spoils. 

Filvanir is an older corsair with an air of unshakeable certainty. She wears the typical corsair’s cloak of sea dragon hide, over armour adorned with jewellery and gold tracery — a calculated reminder to her fellows that she is considerably richer than they. The only creature Filvanir ever treats with affection is her loathsome pet monkey, Heffin.

## **Traits and Talents**
**Hatred (High Elves):** See _Hatred_ in the **WFRP Core Rulebook** . 

**Night Vision:** See clearly for 20 yards and extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards. 

**Catfall:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Athletics Test related to falling or keeping their balance, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Combat Reflexes:** Combat Initiative counts as 80. 

**Dual Wielder:** When fighting with two weapons the character does not have to lose Advantage in order to make a free attack with their second weapon. 

**Furious Assault:** Once per Round, if the character hits an opponent in melee, they may immediately lose Advantage to make an extra attack. 

**Inspiring:** Can influence 5 times the normal number of followers with Leadership Skill during battle. 

**Menacing:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Intimidate Test, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Old Salt:** On successful Row or Sail Tests on the ocean, they may either use their rolled SL, or the number rolled on the units die. They count as two crew towards the minimum number needed to man an ocean-going vessel. 

**Pilot:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Row or Sail Test, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Read/Write:** Can read and write. 

**Strong Swimmer:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Swim Test, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1.

**Attacks**

The fast-talking merchant Anuidethar Veilthorn claims he could sell the Phoenix Crown to Finubar. He does not sell goods, he sells the dream: a personal fortune, a life of comfort, power and influence. Whatever _Nightwake_ is buying or selling, Veilthorn leads negotiations with a subtle blend of charm and carefully concealed threat. 

## **Sword** (49/+8)
**Repeater Handbow and Bolts:** (60/+6) range of 10 yards with the _Impale, Pistol_ , and _Repeater 3_ Qualities, and the _Reload 9_ Flaw 

Veilthorn is a factor, a dark elf merchant. The highborn disdain people such as him, which doesn’t concern Veilthorn so long as he’s getting rich. After all, when they want something precious, they come to him to find it, and he can usually get it through trade or plunder. He’s a self-made elf, who has worked himself up from selling organs on the street in Har Ganeth to travelling the world making deals with the biggest merchants.

Life on _Nightwake_ suits Veilthorn’s buccaneering spirit. He reckons he and Captain Filvanir make a good team, though he feels entitled to a greater share of the profit, and he’s not averse to joining a fight when trade turns to piracy. 

## **Traits and Talents**
**Hatred (High Elves):** See _Hatred_ in the **WFRP Core Rulebook** . 

**Night Vision:** See clearly for 20 yards and extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards. 

Veilthorn takes pride in his appearance, believing trading partners will trust a well-turned-out elf, and dresses in good quality clothing of leather and silk with a fine chainmail vest. He doesn’t realise that his shark-like grin betrays his true intent. 

**Blather:** If challenged about being somewhere they should not be, the character may use their Charm Skill to blather via an **Opposed Charm/Intelligence** Test. Winning causes the opponent to lose track of the conversation, allowing the character to exit the conversation unhindered. 

**Cat-tongued:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Charm Test made to lie, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Dealmaker:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Haggle Test, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Etiquette (High Elves, Scholars):** The characters can blend in socially with the chosen groups, so long as they are dressed and acting appropriately.
